'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
This bundle of pages, cleverly hidden within a rocky crevice at Deserter's March, contain a meticulous set of reports meant to be delivered to someone named [[Harchiand Bronze|H.B.]] The letters record detailed observations of Brotherhood operations starting a few span back. The author appears to have infiltrated the mercenary gang, and spent most of his time helping the Brotherhood establish a base of operations at the Oldwalls near Twin Rivers. 

The spy was able to observe Raetommon on a number of occasions, and notes that the leader has been growing increasingly comfortable in the strange environment and unafraid of disturbing the arcane ruins. In another letter, the agent notes that several Sages were brought to Raetommon, likely unwillingly, in an effort to unravel some of the mysteries of the Oldwalls. As the leader grew more brazen, he also became more paranoid, accusing Brotherhood soldiers of betrayal. 

The last letter appears to have been written in haste, the ink smeared in a number of spots:

"Had to leave. Lifted [[Sage]] notes and magic scrolls to set back enemy plans. R is likely greater threat than thought. Joined wilderness patrols, but absence from Oldwalls will be noticed. Documents hidden, sewn into tunic. Route will intersect with Ironvale. Look for Brother with copper nose ring and scar on left jaw."

==Location==
* [[Deserter's March]]: Hidden under the rocks near the pond at the north-eastern edge. 

==Purpose==
After recovering these notes, return to the pile of Brotherhood bodies in the southwest (where you found the [[Mysterious Missive]] which led you to the notes). Interact to find out that none of the dead there fit the description of the man found in the notes, and that the satchel where the missive was found was slightly damp. With this clue, head to the pool at the centre of the March.

Effect scales. |quality =Superior |material = |cost ={{rings||14|30}} |id =ART_Leather_GLOVE_AlchemistsGloves }} '''Alchemist's Gloves''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''. ==Background== The leather padding surrounding these gloves is dotted with sewn pockets containing herbs, lozenges, and packets of powder commonly found in healing remedies. Gloves like these were originally designed centuries ago by the Archon of Humors, an accomplished magician known in his day for destabilizing the balance of liquids in his enemies. With a flick of his wrist, he would cause internal hemorrhaging, mood adjustments, and unforgettable bowel disruption. Whole battles were won by his spellcasting, which left enemy combatants clutching their guts and leaking uncontrollably. When there wasn't an uprising to quell, the Archon made use of his time improving upon accepted healing techniques. He even invented several of the practices commonly found today. Leeching and the siphoning of fluids came from his influence, and herbs long avoided as poisons were repurposed for purging solutions. Many of his lesser-known advancements in the healing art are of questionable validity, and should be used with caution. ==Locations== * Manufactured at a [[Forge]]. {{rings|1}} {{res|||||10|}} ==Notes== The bonus to [[Control Life]] increases with Renown, up to 60 at Tier 5.{{Navbox artifacts}} [[Category:Gloves]][[Category:Artifacts]][[Category:Artifact gloves]][[Category:Light armor]] [[Category:Forge items]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Bastard's Wound (DLC)|Bastard's Wound]]''.

==Description==
You discovered this ancient parchment deep within the Bastard's Wound Oldwalls, but cannot decipher the notation printed on it. A recruited researcher might help you determine its origins and meaning. 

==Location==
*[[Darkened Hollow]]: On a body in the submerged area to the west.
==Purpose==
To understand the parchment, bring it to [[Sage Garus]] and then agree to hand it over to [[Sirin]] (or just give it to her directly). She will study it, learning the secrets meant only for her. If you havent done it yet, bring her to [[Cairn's Passage|Cairn's passage]]. Afterwards, in Act III her [[Songbird's Bridle]] will be upgraded to an artifact (if you dont burn her notes).

pages.text_en:
Artifacts are powerful magical items that, when wielded, grant their owner a new ability. Artifacts are known throughout the Tiers - and the greater Empire beyond. As an Artifact's reputation grows, its ability becomes more powerful.
Artifacts are carried over to New Game+; 2 artifacts can be selected for inclusion into your inventory on your 1st NG+. The number increases by 1 per new NG+, until a maximum of 9 on your 8th NG+.
Collecting artifacts also increase your fame.


Obtaining artifacts
Weapons
Deathbringer, Heart's Blood and The Baneward: Researched at the Library and then manufactured at the Forge.
Snowfang: Researched using The Silent Archive at the Library and then manufactured at the Forge.
Azure Shield: Found at Gulfglow Oldwalls, possessed by Red-Fang.
Staff of Cairn: Harvest a piece of Cairn during Securing The Sea in the Stone Sea and have it turned into a staff at the Forge.
Dauntless: Infested Oldwalls, embedded in a stone.
Staff of Hours: Burning Library, found near the Silent Archive.
Sunlance:  Twin Rivers Oldwalls - Depths, locked behind the door in the north-eastern corner. Unlock it by powering the beacon with a Saphir Torchkey.
Tempest:  Lethian's Crossing Oldwalls - Antechamber, in the locked chest Zdenya is resting against.
Gravebow: Blade Grave Oldwalls - East, in the closet beyond the beacon room.
Peacemaker: Dropped by Graven Ashe.
Final Scream: Dropped by Voices of Nerat.
Penumbra: Received from Reef-Talon (Bastard's Wound).
Edict's Crescent: Quest reward received from Lycentia for solving Never Free.
Edict's Mallet: Quest reward received from Lohara for solving Never Free.
Wave's Crest: Obtained by talking to Eb once you get the Vial of Inexplicably Heavy Water
Circular Reason: Quest reward for completing Truth and Reconciliation.
Hammer of Sunder: Found at the Burning Library if you end the edict by swapping an artifact.
Wearable gear
Alchemist's Gloves, Commander's Plate, Hierarch's Robes, Nightwalker's Boots: Manufactured at the Forge.
Helm of the First Regent: Found at Rust Canyons, if you proclaimed the Edict with no warning.
Binding of Shadows: Received from Bleden Mark with Favor 3 or dropped by him.
Magebane Helm: Found at Lethian's Crossing, quest item.
Face of Judgment: Dropped by Tunon.
Weeping Whispers: Found at Torn Strand (Bastard's Wound).
Infused Shadows: Examine the murals with Kills-in-Shadow in the Oldwalls under Bastard's Wound.
Songbird's Encore: Obtained at the start of Act 3 by talking to Sirin if you found the Ancient Oldwalls parchment in the Oldwalls
Accessories
Scales of Mercy: Researched using The Silent Archive at the Library and then manufactured at the Forge.
Steadfast Insignia: Found at Oldwalls Breach during A Breach Between Worlds.
Banner of Ardent: Found at the Burning Library if you end the edict by swapping an artifact.


List of artifact weapons


List of artifact equipment
Equipment refers to non-weapon items that can be worn by the characters.

pages.text_en:
Attributes determine the base values of skills. Each skill has a primary and a secondary attribute that contribute towards the skill’s rank. Primary attributes increase the skill by 1.5x the Attribute value, while secondary attributes increase the skill by 0.5x. The One-Handed Weapons skill, for example, uses Might as its primary and Finesse as its secondary. A character with 15 Might and 10 Finesse would have a base One-Handed Weapons skill of 28 ( 15 Might * 1.5 + 10 Finesse * 0.5 ). Attributes also contribute towards secondary statistics, such as the Endurance, Will, and Arcane resistances.
Increasing an attribute costs one point, until the attribute score reaches 19. To raise an attribute from 19 to 29 requires 2 attribute points, and 3 points for 29 to 39, 4 for 39 to 49, and so on. Attribute points are ultimately limited, as character levels are restricted to 99 in New Game+.


List of attributes
Might – your character’s physical strength and attack power.
Finesse – your character’s physical precision.
Quickness – your character’s speed and reaction times.
Vitality – physical health and force of personality.
Wits – intelligence and arcane potential.
Resolve – ability to endure physical and mental challenges.

Bonus scales. |id WPN_ART_SHLD_AzureShield}} '''Azure Shield''' is an [[artifact]] in ''Tyranny''. ==Background== This shield was traditionally an object of ceremonial importance. Champions of [[Azure]] carried it during times of cultural significance - the signing of treaties, declarations of war, meeting of diplomatic envoys and celebrations of past victories. Perhaps its most noted appearance was during the notorious Tarnished Flag incident of 289 TR, when a foreign delegation met on neutral ground and attacked the Azure representatives. The Azure Shield was raised to parry the assassination attempt, and all who stood behind it left the encounter unscathed. Since the fall of Azure, the shield has passed through numerous hands, and presently reeks of Beastwoman musk. ==Location== * [[Stone Sea]]: Carried by [[Red-Fang]] at the [[Gulfglow Oldwalls]]. In the Anarchist path, the Azure Shield is one of four [[artifacts]] which [[Bleden Mark]] want you to find. ==Acquisition== *Disfavored path: Red-Fang is killed as part of [[Securing The Sea]]. *Chorus path: Kill Red-Fang during [[Fangs and Fury]]. *Anarchist path: Red-Fang will give you the Shield if you **kill the Earthshakers at [[Gulfglow Oldwalls]] (which saves you time as you'll need the [[Shard of Pure Azurelith]] from [[Basilon]] for [[The Conquest of Howling Rock]]) OR **kill her OR **demand that she hand over the artifact. This is possible only if you have "helped the Stonestalker tribe" (1 Favor, 0 Wrath, and doing all the side quests without harming any Beastfolk is enough), or are the new Prima. *Rebel path: Kill Red-Fang during [[The Rise of the Earthshakers]]. **Note that you ''cannot'' acquire the Shield if your allies in the [[Stone Sea]] are the [[Stonestalkers]]. {{Navbox weapons}} [[Category:Shields]][[Category:Artifacts]][[Category:Artifact shields]]

'''Banner of Ardent''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
This fraction of the Banner of Peace was worn by the First Speaker of Ardent, a diplomat of the former [[Free Cities]].

The completed assemblage once represented unity in trade and war. The government of [[Ardent]] was wise in the way of contract and treaty negotiation, and ceremonial gestures like these were the currency of the realm. In spite of its magnanimous posturing, Ardent was a place of steep taxes and regulation, and mutually-beneficial trade agreements were seldom available or even possible by design. The very thing that made Ardent strong also made it isolated and vulnerable. Having alienated its neighbors through a series of self-serving commerce deals, no one answered the call for aid when the forces of Kyros amassed at Ardent's borders. The city was taken with little more than a formal missive and terms of peace.

Though the Banner of Ardent is a historical example of conflict resolution achieved prior to the coming of Kyros, it is also frayed on the edges - evidence of being ripped from a larger, more unified mass - which is a more appropriate symbol for the city's legacy.                                 
==Location==
* [[Burning Library]]: Available if you ended the edict of fire by replacing the Silent Archive with another artifact. During Act II, if you chose to save the library, after ending the edict go back to the south west corner of the first floor map, via backtracking from the cavern. The lava has partially receded and you will find several enemies, including a Havoc. The artifact is on a desk.

'''Bindings of Shadows''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
This bracer once worn by Bleden Mark is made of an unfamiliar substance - part velvet-soft darkness and part hardened insect chitin.

It is said that the darkness is more oppressive when an Archon of Shadows walks the face of Terratus. The magic stemming from his power draws on the substance of shadows with an air of welcome and invitation, treating the dark less as something more than an arcane force. As such, a bracer that allows the wearer to embody their darker self has overtones of danger and risk. Just looking at it too closely causes your vision to swim and sends a wave of nausea rolling through your gut.

Bloody Scarlet Fury Armor is an item of equipment in Tyranny.


Background
This leather armor is a unique interpretation of the Scarlet Fury uniform, and shows evidence of heavy use.
New stitches and custom tailoring look designed to maximize flexibility while sacrificing nothing of the intended protection. Verse has sewn trinkets among the padding with care - snippets of hair, fur and claw, pieces of iron and bronze - all likely trophies of previous kills.

'''Commander's Plate''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
This bronze armor is inspired by the garb of the Great Northern Warlords who initially opposed the dominion of Kyros.

The value of this armor cannot measure up to the actual breastplates of the true Warlords, as the wealth of entire realms went into their elaborate forging. Since those deserving of such pieces were few and far between, the old kings and queens of the North were happy to spoil their generals with trappings that required the craft of whole civilizations to assemble - from the complex and intricate metallurgy to the bejeweled fittings and enchantments tailored for the much-celebrated wearer.

In spite of the expenditure of effort and resources, such armor was never handed down the family line, as would be tradition today. If the Warlord's remains were recovered by the home nation, the armor would be ceremonially melted down and destroyed. During the Overlord's conquest of the North, enough such champions died far from home that the knowledge of their armor eventually made its way to the Forge-Bound.

You recognize engravings in the pauldrons as fragments of ancient battle poetry, their full relevance lost along with their language of origin. Whether or not this measures up to the original design, it should be worn with pride.
==Characteristics==
[[Apply the Lash]], [[Will of Command]], [[Call to Battle]], [[Resurgence]] and [[Undying]] talents have their cooldowns reduced by approximately 42%. For example the [[Will of Command]] talent's cooldown is reduced from 1 minute to 35 seconds.

The passphrase needed to remove the barrier to the Silent Archive is recorded on this scroll. The runes glow with arcane light and shift across the parchment from top to bottom.

'First and foremost, for those that have the strength of will, the door to the north shall open.

Secondly comes passion, burning in the south like an unending fire, to provide vitality to the dedicated.

Then from the west shall the one with true resolve come to explain the gravity of commitment to knowledge.

Lastly, look to the east and brace yourself against those who would pull you down. Let your might be solid as stone.'
==Location==
* Received after finding all four [[incomplete passphrase]]s.

pages.text_en:
Consumables is a category of items in Tyranny. Food, potions, and other substances are all consumable items, meaning that they go away when they are used. Every character has several Quick Item slots that represent the consumables that can be used during combat.
Food items provide long-term benefits to the character who eats them, but they're not very strong.
Potions and herbs can be consumed for powerful bonuses that last for a short duration.


List of items


Combat consumables
Consumables that (generally speaking) increase your performance in killing stuff.


Protective
Consumables that protect you from damage in combat.


Healing
All the consumables that heal you or otherwise save you in combat.


Utility
General purpose consumables


Upgrades

'''Corpse-Reaver''' is a [[weapons|weapon]] in ''Tyranny''. 

==Background==
This weathered excuse of a sword started its long career as a cleaver for chopping up dead bodies.

The craftsman had some crude ideas about sanitary corpse disposal and took the initiative on behalf of his small village. After his community rose up against him with charges of desecration, his belongings - including this morbid blade - were lost to history.

{{Infobox weapon |name =Dauntless |image =w_1H_SwordDauntless_L.png |icon = |image size = |artifact = yes |type =[[One-Handed Weapons|One-handed weapon]] |melee =12-15 [[Damage|Slash/Pierce]] vs. Parry |accuracy = +6 |penetration = |recovery = +0.25s |range = |quality = Masterwork |material = |cost = |bonus ='''Resolute''': On critical hit, daze foes for 9.7s in 2m radius
'''Stalwart Surge''': Raise the Dauntless high, releasing a wave of energy to stun all nearby enemies. Damage increases with the Dauntless's Renown. |id =wpn_art_1h_br_sword_dauntless }} '''Dauntless''' is a [[weapons|weapon]] in ''Tyranny''. ==Background== This legendary sword was the badge of office for the Champion of [[Stalwart]]. So many warriors brought Dauntless to battle over the centuries that the presence of the wielder was often less notable than that of the sword itself, which steered the hopes of Stalwart's armies toward victory. Even in instances when a Champion lacked the peoples' confidence, Dauntless made up for their shortcomings by delivering on the promise of victory. The sword's most notable feat of recent memory took place during the Battle of Quelling Field in 398 TR. A Free Cities army advanced on Stalwart's farmlands and nearly won the day. When Dauntless was unsheathed, the defending soldiers broke out in patriotic cheer. This abrupt change of attitude so rattled the Free Cities mercenaries that they assumed their fortunes had changed and that Stalwart had gained a second wind in the battle. It was only days after their panicked retreat that they learned of their error. Consequently, the cultural significance of this blade cannot be underestimated. ==Location== * [[Blade Grave]]: The blade is found at the [[Infested Oldwalls]]; the location is unlocked by interacting with [[Irentis]]. ==Acquisition== *Disfavored path: Irentis is killed as part of [[Breaking the Enemy]]; he holds notes which will unlock the Infested Oldwalls. *Anarchist path: Complete [[Undaunted]], [[Relic Hunter]], and then [[Bound by the Blade]]. On the Anarchist path, Dauntless is one of four [[artifacts]] which [[Bleden Mark]] want you to find. **If you [[Betray Alliance|betray the Chorus at Trapper's Junction]], you'll skip the first two quests, as the Chorus led you straight to Irentis (and [[Mattias]]). *Rebel path: Speak to [[Irentis]] at [[Trapper's Junction]] to add the option of reclaiming the blade during [[A Daunting Path]]. *Chorus path: Similar to the Disfavored path, as Irentis is killed as part of [[A Broken Chord]]. {{Navbox weapons}} {{Navbox artifacts}} [[Category:One-handed weapons]] [[Category:Artifacts]][[Category:Artifact weapons]] [[Category:Bronze weapons]]

All helpful effects on the targets are removed. |id =WPN_ART_1H_OBS_Axe_Deathbringer WPN_ART_2H_OBS_Axe_Deathbringer }} '''Deathbringer''' is an [[artifact]] in ''Tyranny''. ==Background== The [[Forge-Bound]] assembled Deathbringer using materials extracted from the [[Burning Library]]. This axe was inspired by a mighty weapon that lies shattered in the Forge-Bound guildhall. The iron blade had no name, and even that of its creator was lost to time. The known facts amount to stories of a fire that swept through the forges. The smith's conjured flames had whipped into an uncontrollable frenzy, and made the area impassable for several days. Once the flames had cooled, the axe was found in the wreckage - a single crack running down the blade, making the effort and extraordinary results for naught. To this day, the axe is used as an example of art's impermanence. Desiring an equally caustic blade with improved longevity, the Forge-Bound sought to recreate Deathbringer. It is speculated that the obsidian shards dredged from the devastation of the Burning Library retain some echo of power from the [[Edict]] of Fire, which may be the secret to this axe's powers. Not even the Forge-Bound understand Kyros' magic well enough to tell for certain. ==Location== * Manufactured at a [[Forge]] with {{rings|1}} {{res||10 (12 for two-handed variant)||||}} and 4 recruits, [[Plans: Deathbringer]] and [[Obsidian Fragment]]. {{Navbox weapons}} {{Navbox artifacts}} [[Category:One-handed weapons]][[Category:Artifacts]][[Category:Artifact weapons]] [[Category:Forge items]]

'''Edict of Execution''' kills all in a designated area if the conditions specified in the Edict are not met.
==Effects==
* The Overlord has decreed that all in the valley on Kyros' Day of Swords shall die unless Kyros' representative holds Ascension Hall. Note that it's perfectly possible to rest until ''after'' Kyros' Day of Swords before the Edict is pronounced. In this case, the Edict will function as intended, except the Execution date will be set a ''year'' away. The Overlord did not specify the ''year'', after all.

==Historical==
*In the year 431 TR, The Overlord [[kyros|Kyros]] proclaimed an [[Edict]] over [[vendrien's well|Vendrien's Well]]: "Those who defy Our just and lawful Order are traitors to Our Empire. Those who fail in their duty to bring justice to traitors are, in Our eyes, equally treasonous. Let Our armies prove their good faith by retaking [[vendrien's well|Vendrien's Well]] from those who defy Our Will. Unless Our representative holds the Hall of Ascension on [[Kyros' Day|Our Day of Swords]], all in the valley of [[vendrien's well|Vendrien's Well]] shall perish."

'''Edict of Fire''' brings the energy of Fire to large regions of the world. This generates incredible heat - sometimes Flame - as well as strengthening the powers of magic.
==Effects==
*Tiny pools of lava and molten magma begin to peek out of the broken earth in and around the land. Volatile lava traps hazard the area. The party receives a reduction to Fire [[damage]] and all characters have their magic skill increased. [[Bane]] in the area are empowered.
*Exhausting desert like heat withers the region and dries up all natural sources of water. All characters have their magic skill increased. The Fatebinder's party also heals a portion of Frost damage received and consumables are far more effective. Foes become Fatigued and have a penalty to [[Quickness]].
*Steam jets periodically out of porous pockets in the earth and canyons in the region. Rivers, lakes, and other sources of water are heated to a near boiling temperature. All characters have their Resolve penalized and their magic skills increased. Bane in the area become more powerful and afflictions caused by the Fatebinder's party last longer. Water and steam burn both allies and foes.
*Black ash and wisps of tiny orange embers litter the air, aimlessly floating and drifting about. All characters in the region are imbued with an increase in magic skill and a greater increase in [[Control Fire]] skill. The party gains an increase to Burn damage that is dealt and all melee attacks from party members apply a small amount of Burn damage.

==Historical==
*In the year 430 TR, [[Kyros]] the Overlord proclaimed an [[Edict]] over the [[Vellum Citadel]] in the Contested Lands: 'It is Our most solemn duty to protect the citizens of Our Empire from all dangers, including the danger of Knowledge that is Forbidden. Let those who, in their burning arrogance, hold tightly to this lore be consumed by Our wrath. Therefore, let the fires of Terratus rise up and consume them for as long as forbidden knowledge lies within the heart of the [[Vellum Citadel]].' With this Edict, the Citadel became known as the [[Burning Library]].

'''Edict of Malediction''' will twist the strands of Fate, causing misfortune and bad luck to plague your enemies.
==Effects==
*	The balance of fates is shifted for all those within the region. The party gains a bonus to all skills, Graze Precision and Hit Precision. Foes have a penalty to all skills and a portion of their critical hits are converted to hits and hits are converted to grazes.

==Location==
*Has to be researched in the [[Library]].

[[Category:Edicts]]

[[File:edict_image_shadow.png|center]]
'''Edict of Nightfall''' brings permanent darkness to the land. Plants will wither, animals will sicken, and people will slowly freeze without the sun's warmth.
==Effects==
*	Darkness plagues the region, regardless of the time of day. The party gains a bonus to [[Subterfuge]] and [[damage]]. While foes receive a penalty to perception range and Accuracy. Foes are also Blinded at the start of combat.

==Historical==
* Kyros conquered Ikenar Pass by casting the Edict in 282 TR. The endless night results in a popular uprising that deposes the rules of Ikenar and brings it into the fold.<ref>[[Lantry]]: "''I've read of an [[Edict]] cast on Ikenar Pass in 282. [[Kyros]]' magic ushered in endless night, well endless until the inhabitants slew their own rulers, or so the [[Edict]] was worded.''"</ref>
==Location==
*Given by [[Bleden Mark]] in the Anarchist path.

'''Edict of Stone''' leeches magical energy from the sky and living creatures, storing it in the rocks below. This energy can lead to earthquakes and the slow petrification of the living.
==Effects==
*	A stone curse plagues the region. Blood, flesh, and nature begin to harden over time, causing petrification and slowed movement. The Edict lowers the potency of magic in the area and weakens the [[Bane]].
*	Tremors and earthquakes plague the region. Periodic rumbles and shifting cause characters to fall Prone in combat. All character have [[Control Stone|Stone Magic]] skill increased. The party gains an increase to Prone defense, while foes have Prone durations increased.
*	Howling winds echo through the canyons of the Stone Sea, driving Beastmen mad from the constant echoes. Movement becomes difficult for all those in the area and defenses are lowered for foes. The Fatebinder's party benefits from an increased Dodge and Parry while in the storm.
*	Rain of corrosive acid falls from the sky. All characters have their armor reduced and have chaotic elemental damage added to their attacks. The party gains a corrosive damage effect on their attacks, while enemies have their weapons corroded, reducing attack damage.

==Historical==
*In the last year of [[Kyros]]' conquest, when the Archon [[Cairn]] rebelled against the Overlord's rule, an [[Edict]] was proclaimed upon the realm of [[Azure]]: 'To preserve Our Peace, the promise of safety to our citizens, all Archons must submit to Our will. Any Archon who refuses proper Submission must be brought to justice. Therefore, let the foundations of Azure be shattered and life drain from the land while the traitor [[Cairn]] draws breath.' With this Edict, [[Azure]] became known as the [[Stone Sea]].
{{navbox edicts}}
[[Category:Edicts]]

[[File:edict_image_storms.png|center]]
'''Edict of Storms''' generates a massive storm that covers huge areas of the world. The chaotic energy unleashed will cause random damage to strike your enemies during combat.
==Effects==
*The storms of rust howling through the Blade Grave reduce your visibility slightly, but grant bonuses to your ranged attacks. Enemy ranged attacks are hindered.
*The winds of Kyros' Edict fill the air with thick clouds of rust from the decaying weapons and armor that litter the ground. No natural wind, it hampers your every movement.

==Historical==
*In the year 430 TR, the Overlord proclaimed an [[Edict]] over the Realm of [[Stalwart]]: 'Those who, in pride and arrogance, stand against the peace and order of Our Empire shall be ground beneath the stones of their land. Let those who call themselves [[Unbroken]], who embrace the chaos of war in defiance of Our Order, be broken in the storms of Our Rage. Let Our storm rage until the last blade be broken, or the line of Regent falls.' With this Edict, Stalwart became known as the [[Blade Grave]].
{{navbox edicts}}
[[Category:Edicts]]

The '''Edict of Tumult''' was unleashed against [[Setting-Sun]] in 429 TR, in retaliation for its continued resistance against the Overlord. The Overlord's words  stirred the winds, and shook the land. A terrible wall of water rose from the sea, blotting out the sky before entirely swallowing the city and much of the coast. The other Free Cities were quick to surrender.<ref>[[Fatebinder Calio]]</ref>

If you proclaimed the [[Edict of Stone]] during the [[Conquest]] instead of [[Fatebinder Calio]], she proclaimed the {{Pagename nd}}. If you didn't, it's possible she still did, but it may have fallen to whichever of [[Fatebinder Rhogalus|Rhogalus]] or [[Fatebinder Nunoval|Nunoval]] is skipped (the former if you read [[Edict of Fire|Fire]] and the latter for [[Edict of Storms|Storms]])

Kyros' most powerful magic is that of the '''Edict''', commandments cast upon whole regions that can control and destroy man and nature alike. Once cast, an Edict can rain fire, wither crops, demoralize cities, usher in endless night, or do whatever it is that Kyros envisioned. No known force, magical or mundane can stop an Edict, though each Edict is often worded to include some condition or contingency that will see its end.

Some Edicts have been short lived, delivering days of wanton catastrophe. Just as many have lingered for centuries.

For details on your Edicts, see [[Mysterious device]].

==Overview==
The power of Kyros is like none other. The mightiest Archons fail to match it, and no magician's spell approaches the sheer magnitude of an Edict. It can wipe cities from the land, collapse mountains into the sea, and blight entire nations. It can linger for centuries or be as brief as a few minutes of devastation. Most notably, Edicts respond directly to changes in the state of the world, even its intangible and metaphysical variables, ending when specific circumstances come to pass. They're best described as physical manifestations of the Overlord's will. Anything beyond that is a matter for arcanists and philosophers. It's not known how Kyros manages to extend that will through Fatebinders, with some speculating it might bear some semblance to when [[Graven Ashe]] extends his protection to his troops... Or perhaps the hierarchy of the realm itself allows the Overlord to channel power through them. What is known is that while reading an Edict is no small honor, it can also be a veritable death sentence. Even if the reader survives the torrential power that the Overlord's words channel through them, they then have to contend with surviving the effects they unleash upon the world.

==List of Edicts==
*[[Edict of Execution]]: This Edict kills all in a designated area if any of the specified conditions fail.
*[[Edict of Fire]]: The Edict of Fire brings the energy of Fire to large regions of the world. This generates incredible heat - sometimes Flame - as well as strengthening the powers of magic.
*[[Edict of Malediction]]: The Edict of Malediction will twist the strands of Fate, causing misfortune and bad luck to plague your enemies.	
*[[Edict of Nightfall]]: The Edict of Nightfall brings permanent darkness to the land. Plants will wither, animals will sicken, and people will slowly freeze without the sun's warmth.	
*[[Edict of Stone]]: The Edict of Stone leeches magical energy from the sky and living creatures, storing it in the rocks below. This energy can lead to earthquakes and the slow petrification of the living.
*[[Edict of Storms]]: This Edict bombards the lands with a violent storm. 	
==Historical Edicts==
* Edict of Sorrows, broken by Golbraith in 110 TR
* Edict of Twisting Grasses, broken in 380 TR
* [[Edict of Tumult]], issued against [[Setting-Sun]] in 429 TR: A massive wave of wind and water crashes on the targeted area.
*Edict of Dust, issued against the whole of Terratus in 11 TR and notably causing the extinction of Antelopes.
==Exploits==
Although few have tried (or even dared) to exploit Kyros's Edicts, the [[Young Fatebinder]] can do so.
*[[Edict of Execution]]: In Act I, the Young Fatebinder can delay the proclamation of this Edict till ''after'' the Day of Swords. This extends the deadline of the Edict by many times.
*[[Edict of Storms]]: In Act II, by allowing an abdication via verbal renunciation, the Young Fatebinder can lift the Edict while preventing the death of a young life, as opposed to the Overlord's wishes.
*[[Edict of Fire]]: Also in Act II, by physically moving a source of forbidden knowledge, the Young Fatebinder can lift the Edict.

By lifting Edicts, the Fatebinder's [[belief|fame]] increases, and they learn how to [[Mysterious device|cast the Edicts themselves]].

==Description==
Elixirs of Finesse are imbibed to train a soldier's precision and accuracy. They are extremely rare and incredibly valuable as a result.
The problem of keeping troops awake during an extended campaign is as old as warfare itself, and alchemists have experimented on captives and brave volunteers to pin down the best solution. Their early results were promising, but over time proved detrimental to a soldier's aim, coordination, and even sanity. The present formula, mixed with a hearty Stalwart herb, succeeded in its goal with the surprising result of augmenting one's physical and mental acuity.

==Description==
The Elixir of Quickness improves the imbiber's natural combat and spellcasting speed.
The formula stems from Kyros' years spent subjugating the northern continent. The Overlord's forces clashed with a rebellious mountain tribe, whose tactics elegantly depended upon rushing downhill to face the enemy, maintaining the high ground at any cost. Kyros' forces grew keen to the strategy and littered the enemy's approach with trenches, pits, and caltrops. When the tribe eventually submitted, they revealed that their prowess came from a shaman-brewed potion that sped up reaction time. Running downhill was just an old trick to build up courage. The army was happy to appropriate the recipe for their own use, and it has proven a critical asset in every subsequent campaign.
==Location==
*[[Cacophony]]: In a locked chest ([[Subterfuge]] ??) behind [[Voices of Nerat]]'s throne.

'''Face of Judgment''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
This mask of stern and unforgiving iron was previously worn by Tunon the Adjudicator as a symbol of impartiality.

Even before he assumed his mantle of Archon and lawbringer, Tunon's obsession with fair procedure extended to his face, which he did not trust to audience a trial without expressing some unintended bias. This mask replaced a previous variation made of wood, and was assigned to Tunon when he became the Archon of Justice.

In keeping with Tunon's severity, his mask is extremely uncomfortable. How he wore this for uninterrupted centuries is a mystery. His mask is nothing if not an extension of one of his core philosophies: that everyone should feel protected under Kyros' Law, but no one should feel safe.

==Location==
* [[Tunon's Court]]: Worn by Tunon.

Fatebinder of Tunon armor is an item of equipment in Tyranny.


Background
The leather raiment assigned to Tunon's elite lawbringers is prominently decorated with the Court's sigil.
Court garments are fitted to their owners with care, and no two are exactly alike. Minor variations in design and tailoring reflect something of the wearer, whose devotion to the Archon of Law is recognized and celebrated by the very right to don such finery.


Location
Received at the beginning of the game, depending on your skill choices. All issued gear is distinguished by the prefix Ceremonial, but is otherwise identical to regular variants.
Superior versions can be purchased from Revos at the Mountain Spire.

==Background==
Headgear worn by Tunon's Fatebinders are made to withstand extreme weather conditions.
As agents of the Court are prone to visiting regions struck by Kyros' Edicts, their garb must be resilient and adaptable by necessity. The leatherwork protects the head from harm while insulating against cold, but offers sufficient space to breathe in environments of extreme heat.
==Location==

Duration of afflictions scales with Renown. |id =WPN_ART_1H_BR_Scepter_FinalScream }} '''Final Scream''' is an Artifact [[weapons|weapon]] in ''Tyranny''. ==Background== This scepter has been wielded by the Voices of Nerat, and by all accounts has never known a second owner. Who crafted such a monstrous weapon is a matter of speculation, and it isn't beyond possibility that the Voices himself was responsible in some bygone era. Rumors circulate that the screaming mouth at the head contains the agonized howls of the Archon's family, who he tortured to death in the early years of Kyros' dominion as an act of fealty. The earliest mentions of Final Scream came from a chronicler who attended many of the public executions the Voices hosted. After a prolonged interrogation session, the Voices would finish his work by unveiling his scepter and bashing in the skull of his victim. Other accounts tell that when the Archon of Secrets rooted out treachery in the Empire, he would have Final Scream delivered as a ""gift"" (really a warning) to the household of the offender. Within the fortnight, he would pay the traitors a visit to retrieve his property, which often included members of the family. Some have interpreted this behavior as an invitation for the guilty to flee and grant the Voices the thrill of the hunt. The open eyes and mouth reveal a core of the Archon's signature green flames, which yet smolder with some semblance of his fractured awareness. ==Location== * Carried by [[The Voices of Nerat]] {{Navbox weapons}} {{Navbox artifacts}} [[Category:One-handed weapons]] [[Category:Artifacts]] [[Category:Artifact weapons]] [[Category:Bronze weapons]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is one of six [[attributes]] in ''Tyranny''.

==Effects==
The Finesse attribute describes a character's physical and mental precision. Finesse is used to determine accuracy of attacks and spells, as well as increasing worn armor's chances to reduce a hit type (e.g. a critical to a hit, or a hit to a graze).
==Modifiers==
;Adding or removing a point changes the values by the following value.
* +/-1% to Armor Deflection
*  +/-3 to Accuracy

=== Skills ===
Finesse is the primary attribute for the skills [[Bows]], [[Athletics]], [[Unarmed Combat]], [[Parry]], and [[Control Gravelight]]  (1.5 skill points per point of Finesse), and secondary (0.5 skill points) for [[One-Handed Weapons]], [[Dual Wield]], and [[Magic Staff]].{{navbox charsys}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
[[sage|Sage]] Torven,

[[kyros|Kyros]]’ armies have been rebuffed for now, but it is only a temporary victory. I have no doubt that we may hold these walls a good deal longer, but you must remember that the Overlord aims not to butcher the Citadel’s keepers, but to destroy its secrets. [[kyros|Kyros]] is not omnipotent. Her powers may be known and understood in time, and she rightly fears the knowledge we hoard here.

The Silent Archive must be protected. There is no library in the Tiers that is its equal! Nothing else matters. Nothing. We may not know the Overlord’s plans, but, with time and research, we can circumvent any of her designs. I need you to ensure that we will have that time when the moment is right.

Focus your efforts on [[sage|Sage]] Steya’s theoretical forays into temporal magic. While we were right to deny such dangerous experimentation before, now is the time in which its risks are justified. Gather the Elder Sages and make your way to the lower chambers. You are to remain there until you devise a solution to Steya’s problem of scale. Halting the flow of time in a single chamber won’t be sufficient if [[kyros|Kyros]] drowns us all in a storm or hurtles this library into the firmament. You must find a way to encase all of the Citadel in such a spell, should disaster come.

Your success isn’t optional. This library will be a distant memory if [[kyros|Kyros]] has her way. Should we both survive, I will be happy to congratulate you on your breakthrough. Until then, get to work.

-First [[sage|Sage]] Arwel

9 vs. Pierce/Frost |damage = |recovery = +1.2s |effect = |ability = |quality =Common |material =Iron |cost ={{rings||2}} |id =iron_armor_barik }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item of equipment in ''[[Tyranny]]''. ==Background== Barik's iron shell is a disorderly fusion of rusted scrap from at least a hundred warped breastplates and twice as many swords. That this heap of lethal garbage fused around Barik's torso in a rough approximation of armor without destroying him in the process is either a remarkable coincidence or an arcane achievement beyond the comprehension of any smithy. Aside from the omnipresent stench of oil and rust, the reek of a long-unwashed body and pools of stagnant bodily fluids oppress the air around Barik. Barik's armor is a hideous amalgamation of once-fine iron suits, long since rusted and fused together. There is no telling how many pieces of war-torn scrap contributed to this mighty gear, or how many layers it comprises. Any evident buckles or straps that would permit removal are missing. Patterns of spikes among the shoulders and elbows, bent into some crude alignment, contribute to the suit's battle-readiness and intimidation. The smell wafting from between plates suggests it has been worn for some time. ==Location== * Fused to [[Barik]]. {{Navbox Body armors}} [[Category:heavy armor]][[Category:Iron items]][[Category:Body armor]]

{{Infobox equipment |image =Iron_BOOTS_Barik_L.png |icon = |image size = |type =Heavy Armor ([[Barik]] only), Boots |armor =1.5
0 vs. Crush/Fire
2.25 vs. Pierce/Frost |damage = |recovery = +0.5s |effect = |ability = |quality =Common |material =Iron |cost ={{rings||1}} |id =iron_boots_barik }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item of equipment in ''[[Tyranny]]''. ==Background== The pieces of fused iron that encapsulate Barik's legs are merely an abstract representation of boots. Worn-down sections of rust under his feet appear the result of marching across great distances and patient hours spent filing sections down for the sake of balance. Articulation is either due to coincidence or prolonged effort bending at fused iron, but the result is the same: Barik can stand and move with some semblance of normalcy. Barik's boots look to have collected the scrap and detritus of several battle. They creak with his shifting weight, and rust has all but enveloped the misshapen parts. ==Location== * Fused to [[Barik]]. {{Navbox Bootss}} [[Category:heavy armor]][[Category:Iron items]][[Category:Boots]]

{{Infobox equipment |image =Iron_GLOVE_Barik_L.png |icon = |image size = |type =Heavy Armor ([[Barik]] only), Gloves |armor =1.5
0 vs. Crush/Fire
2.25 vs. Pierce/Frost |damage =15-18 Crush vs. Parry |recovery = +0.5s |effect = |ability = |quality =Common |material =Iron |cost ={{rings||1}} |id =iron_glove_barik }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item of equipment in ''[[Tyranny]]''. ==Background== Barik's gauntlets are fused around his hands like vicious talons. They branch up his arms in a continuous line of interconnected iron that join up with the rest of his armor, forming a single coherent piece. His fingers are fully articulated, and he flexes them often - perhaps to remind himself that they are present. Barik's hands are monstrous protrusions expressed in iron. His knuckles are adorned with unforgiving spikes, and each digit tapers with a talonlike curl. Barik looks to have modified the grip for wielding a weapon, but his gauntlets are unsuited to more delicate work. ==Location== * Fused to [[Barik]]. {{Navbox gloves}} [[Category:heavy armor]][[Category:Iron items]][[Category:Gloves]]

It hides his face, allowing only a suggestion of visible detail behind the obscurity. An accumulation of rust has gathered just under the eye slits. ==Location== * Fused to [[Barik]]. {{Navbox Headgears}} [[Category:heavy armor]][[Category:Iron items]][[Category:Headgear]]

Considerable effort has gone into the uniformity of each of the tooth-like notches, suggesting the devotion and intentionality of a true artist. All the same, merely holding the blade overwhelms you with the reality that this instrument has caused suffering on an unimaginable scale. This sword's name would suggest mercy and restraint, but it would be mercy to strike a victim down at once, and restraint would only prolong suffering at the tip of this blade. Better to deliver death quickly than with a gentle touch. ==Location== * Carried by [[Voices of Nerat]]. {{Navbox weapons}} [[Category:One-handed weapons]] [[Category:Bronze weapons]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Bastard's Wound (DLC)|Bastard's Wound]]''.

==Description==
The Beastmen members of the Freeblade Marauders carry small effigies of twig and grass in the rough shape of humans. Though they do not speak of the significance of the figures, with each foe they slay in battle they add another twig or tress of grass. The oldest, most successful Beasts wear their effigies, nigh-spherical bundles of bramble, proudly about their necks.

These effects scale with Renown. |id =WPN_ART_2H_SP_BOW_Gravebow Superior }} '''Gravebow''' is an [[artifact]] in ''Tyranny''. ==Background== Gravebow is such a storied weapon that it was long ago written off as a myth. As many contradictory stories of its origin exist as those of its previous users and final resting place. The more recent claim that an Archon of Turmoil wielded the bow in a war to single-handedly destroy the Bane. Some accounts posit that hundreds of bows of differing power share the title of "Gravebow," which has confused the weapon's history and deeds over time. The oldest claim that Gravebow predates the Oldwalls themselves, though none of these claims can be substantiated. A poem claimed to have been taken by charcoal rubbing at the exterior of an Oldwalls posits that Gravebow might one day loose an arrow with such force that the Oldwalls themselves will crumble, and the surrounding Spires will fall like matchsticks. The validity of the source is questionable at best, as the author presented no rubbing and failed to recall the site in which he took it. Whatever else Gravebow might be, its string thrums and pulses with energy desperate to be released. ==Location== * [[Blade Grave Oldwalls - East]]: Beyond the beacon room. ==Gallery== Gravebow (Masterwork).png {{Navbox weapons}} {{Navbox artifacts}} [[Category:Bows]][[Category:Artifacts]][[Category:Artifact weapons]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item   in ''[[Tales from the Tiers]]''. 
==Background==
Soldiers in the Overlord's legions sometimes refer to the Unification of Terratus as 'The Endless March,' a campaign without end. Wise officers curb use of this phrase, recognizing the danger in suggesting aloud that Kyros' conquest will never see its conclusion. As light and comfortable as they are protective, these masterfully-crafted boots seem designed to ensure a faster end to the fighting.

Healing scales with Renown. |id =WPN_ART_1H_IR_Dagger_HeartsBlood }} '''Heart's Blood''' is an [[artifact]] in ''Tyranny''. ==Background== The handle of Heart's Blood is tightly wrapped with cords of severed human tendons, and the blade itself is curved at an angle that encourages open wounds. This crude design was the product of a mage who translated the pre-Empire runes on the surface of a battered shield. To his surprise, he discovered a poem, though much of the context and meaning were lost: Heart's Blood, Urgent to spill, open, drink, Grant us the boon of your delight. The mage recognized the rune for "blood" to correspond with a contemporary Archon, suggesting there was power in the name. He spent the remainder of his career puzzling out the theory behind a blade that fit the shield - an effort that yielded the early properties of this weapon, and a mystery left dormant until now. Those who hold Heart's Blood are consumed by waves of eagerness, and the need to plunge the blade into an enemy's guts at times becomes overwhelming. Whatever dark heritage first conceived of this misshapen weapon, it is now awake to embrace its destiny. ==Location== * Researched and manufactured at [[Spires]] ([[Library]] and [[Forge]]). '''Hierarch's Robes''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
The Forge-Bound initially conceived of the Hierarch's Robes as a means of protecting their smiths from the dangers of conjured flame.

Weaving together fragments of cloth from disparate mage guilds produced a result altogether more useful than they could have imagined: a protective garment that combines the tolerances of otherwise distinct arcane traditions.
Robes like these were similarly assembled by Ponto the Agglomerate, a resentful mage who had been rejected by most of the major guilds and thought himself superior to the arcane establishment. He set off into the wilderness with the aim of founding his own course of study, and was not seen for many years. He later reappeared while breaking into the chambers of Mage Guild elders, cutting at their robes and murdering those who caught him in the frenzied act.

The legalities of his "research" were put into question. Some argued that the right of Magician's Folly protected Ponto from punishment, but Kyros' Peace was also to be upheld. In the end, a coterie of apprentices from disparate Guilds assembled at Ponto's last known hiding spot and "accidentally" bombarded it with arcane force, within their rights destroying all but a few ragged strips of cloth.

==Location==
* Manufactured at a [[Forge]] after researching [[Plans: Hierarch's Robes]].

pages.text_en:
Every character has 6 wearable equipment slots: Head, Chest, Gloves, Feet, and two Accessory slots. Each item equipped in one of these slots benefits the character in several ways, including Armor, Deflection, and bonuses to certain skills.


Classification
Equippable items fit into different broad categories: Cloth, Leather, Bronze, and Iron. Each of these provide different benefits. Some Talents require a character to have a certain type of item equipped before they will activate, such as requiring that a character wear only Light armor (Cloth or Leather).
In addition, characters have several Quick Item slots for consumables. These slots represent the food, potions, and other substances the character has at the top of their pack. These are the consumable items a character can use during combat. The Bandolier talent upgrades the number of Quick Item slots every character has access to.


Accessories
Every character has two slots dedicated to wearing Accessory items. These items are not visible on the character, but provide bonuses while equipped. Many Accessories are magical items that increase a character's Attributes, skills, or defenses.


Quality
Items in Tyranny have one of five Quality ratings: Common, Fine, Superior, Exquisite, and Masterwork. As an item's quality rating improves, so do its effects. Weapons deal more damage, Armor becomes more protective, etc. Item quality can be improved with the Forge upgrade.
Items of Common, Fine, and Superior Quality can be found on the bodies of enemies or in stores throughout Tyranny. Some locked chests will contain the occasional Exquisite item. The only way to obtain a Masterwork item is to improve it yourself.


Weapon sets
Every character has up to four Weapon Sets they can swap between during combat. All characters start with two Weapon Sets available. The Abundant Arms Talent allows all party members to access additional Weapon Sets.
Each Weapon Set requires a Primary Weapon. If that Primary Weapon is Two Handed (e.g. large swords or maces, a magic staff, or a bow), then no additional items can be added to the Weapon Set. If the Primary Weapon is One Handed (e.g. small swords, daggers, or thrown javelins) then a Secondary Item can be added to the Weapon Set (e.g. a shield or a second One Handed weapon).
Shields are Off-hand weapons, meaning they can only be equipped in the Secondary slot within a Weapon Set. Characters can swap between Weapon Sets during combat, but will incur a Recovery Penalty for doing so.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
This hunk of wrought iron is used to sear the counter-clockwise twist into the flesh of Scarlet Chorus recruits. Those who cannot endure the searing mark are deemed unfit for even the most menial chore in the Chorus, and such unfit recruits become teamsters or corpses, depending on their capacity for manual labor. You can sell this to a merchant as spare parts.

Fashioned in great number by the overworked smiths of the Candle Mountains, each recruitment brand has its own unique size and style of curl, as well imperfections and deformities that come from the hurried fabrication process. The lack of a uniform brand creates cliques amongst the Scarlet Chorus - all recruits that share the same brand share memories of being burned and marked for life by the same person.
==Location==
* [[Trapper's Junction]]: Carried by [[Jagged Remedy]].

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
This missive is written in a shaky but impassioned scrawl that left deep creases in the parchment:

Remedy,

The [[Unbroken]] have been most troublesome for Ashe and his inbred legion. Invite as many of their number to join our song as you can. Pay special attention to their leader, [[Mattias]], and bring him to [[Cacophony]] in one piece. We know how you love to cut into tendons and play the puppeteer, but humor us this once with your restraint.

~[[Voices of Nerat|Your Adoring Leader]]

==Location==
* [[Trapper's Junction]]: Carried by [[Jagged Remedy]].

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a  support skill in ''Tyranny''.
==Description==
Lore skill determines a character's ability to decipher information and put together clues from fragments of information. This skill is critical for magic users who wish to learn new [[sigils]] to power their [[spells]]. Lore is also used in dialogue to determine what you know about the history of the world or to impress others with your intelligence.

Compared to other support skills, Lore checks give the least amount of experience points, which is probably to be expected, as it is relatively easy to improve the skill via spellcasting. Therefore, before you choose to use this check, consider your audience; some characters do not appreciate you flaunting your knowledge.

'''Magebane Helm''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
The Forge-Bound crafted this helmet to ward the settlement of [[Lethian's Crossing]] from the [[Magebane]].

The iron is polished to a fine sheen, and the [[sigils]] inscribed in the dark metal glow with power. The forces of [[Kyros]] have long eschewed ceremonial totems in favor of more practical items. A statue or otherwise more abstract symbol could invite analysis or interpretation, while a helmet is straightforward and nothing more or less than what it is.

Even within the pragmatic confines of their art, the [[Forge-Bound]] seek perfection through iron. Enchantments are lovingly hammered into ore, and the shape of a piece is ushered through intentional stages of development.

==Characteristics==
A powerful protective garment. Stealing it will reduce the ability of Lethian's Crossing to resist invasion, affecting the [[Tyranny endings|ending]]. In the Anarchist path, the Helm is one of four [[artifacts]] which [[Bleden Mark]] want you to find. Remember that if you wish to let the Crossing have the Helm, you can show the Helm to Mark first, ''before'' speaking to [[Eldian]].

==Location==
* [[Lethian's Crossing]]: Created by [[Zdenya]]. Found on [[Raetommon]] at [[Lethian's Crossing Oldwalls - Antechamber]] during [[Forbidden Passage]] (Disfavored path) and its equivalent on other paths.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
This map indicates the purported location of the Helm of the First Regent. Its owner, a high-ranking Regent known as Epistratos, was killed during the initial destructive wave brought about by the [[edict|Edict]] of Storms. Elia's notes on this map lament his fate, one which could have been avoided had the Fatebinder given some advance warning of the [[edict|Edict]] to come. Her last words indicate that the helm is likely in Rust Canyons itself, as she recovered Epistratos' banner near a spiral-shaped blade formation.
==Location==
* [[Rust Canyons]]: Carried by [[Elia]]. Only found if no warning was given to Stalwart.

'''Might''' is one of six [[attributes]] in ''Tyranny''.

==Effects==
Might determines the physical strength of a character. Increased Might leads to more powerful attacks and stronger abilities, as well as increasing the Endurance defense.

==Modifiers==
;Adding or removing points changes the values by the following value.
* +/-3% to Attack and Ability Strength per point
* +/-3 to Endurance Defense

=== Skills ===
Might is the primary attribute for the skills [[One-Handed Weapons]], [[Control Stone]], [[Control Vigor]], and [[Two-Handed Weapons]], and [[Eb|Eb's]] skill [[Tidecasting]] (1.5 skill points per point of Might), and secondary (0.5 skill points) for[[Bows]] and [[Athletics]].

'''Nightwalker's Boots''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
These dark and supple boots are made from the hide of a powerful Beastman hunter.

Some of what the Beast possessed in life endures in death, which has been augmented by runes pertaining to the Archon of Shadows. In addition to Bleden Mark's name, less recognizable sigils seem to glow with power, though fall short of disrupting the darkness.

One familiar rune corresponds to the name of an Archon of Shadows who was a purported Beastwoman herself - a peerless stalker and trapper who eschewed human civilization and lived for untold centuries. It was said that she moved from one wilderness to the next, working her way through the local prey until she was the uncontested Alpha, and would then move on - intent on becoming the dominion over all nature.

Whether Kyros proved her wrong or she still lurks in the wilderness is a matter of speculation.

==Location==
* Manufactured at a [[Forge]] with {{rings|1||}} {{res|||||6}} and 6 recruits plus the [[Hound's Hide Mantle]].

==Description==
Determines effectiveness of attacks using weapons wielded in one hand. Higher skill values lead to more accurate attacks and more critical strikes.
==Affected weapons==
* Any one-handed sword, dagger, mace, hammer, axe. This includes thrown weapons.

==Increasing the skill==
* By using one-handed weapons in combat
* By finding NPC-teachers
* By asking your party members to share experience

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Bastard's Wound (DLC)|Bastard's Wound]]''.

==Description==
These ragged-edged scraps of thin vellum appear to be copied pages of the Screed, a philosophical text popular among the poorer classes within the Tiers. The Screed supposedly vilifies the nobility as rapacious laggards only possessed of their position and influence by dint of circumstance, worse than honest criminals and to be resisted at every opportunity. Only a handful of people could actually read the Screed, most recited it by (approximate) memory from someone else and over the years, dozens of variations of the Screed appeared, each with their own idiosyncratic rants regarding whichever axe the particular author wished to grind.

The limbs of this bow originate from a thorny bramble wielded only by the brave.

==Description==
An acolyte of the Archon Thousand Embers, founder of the School of Wild Wrath, the erratic Paulex plagued the southwestern Tiers with wildfires almost five centuries ago. Notoriously indecisive, the Wrathcaster commissioned a pair of thin, light bracers that wouldnâ€™t hinder him from drawing a new weapon at a moment's notice. Though the actual bracers used by Paulex have been lost, no few reproductions have been crafted from the original design.
==Location==
*[[Sentinel Stand Outskirts]]; During [[The Weight of Aegis|Weight of the Aegis]] quest armor part retrieval. Damage scales with Renown. |id =WPN_ART_2H_IR_Mace_Peacemaker Superior }} '''Peacemaker''' is an [[artifact]] in ''Tyranny''. ==Background== Before he became an Archon, [[Graven Ashe]] wielded Peacemaker in service to his king. Each of the Great Northern Warlords was gifted a weapon of extraordinary power, and all of them (save this one) are said to hang in [[Kyros]]' trophy gallery. In spite of its age, the iron is lovingly preserved and treated with regular applications of oil. The word "ABSOLUTION" is carved down the length of the haft in runes that predate Kyros' dominion. It can be inferred that Ashe added this personal touch after his fall to disfavor, though he would never achieve what he sought. The Great General kept Peacemaker close at all times, and shared its history with no one. Legends dating back centuries imply that its lightning-wreathed head changed its aspect every hundred years - cycling between fire, water, storm and Gravelight in no discernible order. Even the name - Peacemaker - is a topic of scrutiny. The name only became a matter of record after Ashe surrendered to Kyros- implying that Ashe made his peace when he laid the hammer at Kyros' feet. ==Location== * Carried by [[Graven Ashe]]. {{Navbox weapons}} {{Navbox artifacts}} [[Category:Iron weapons]][[Category:Two-handed weapons]][[Category:Artifacts]][[Category:Artifact weapons]]

pages.wikitext_en:
Items in Tyranny have one of five '''Quality''' ratings: Common, Fine, Superior, Exquisite, and Masterwork. As an item's quality rating improves, so do its effects. Weapons deal more damage, Armor becomes more protective, etc. Item quality can be improved with the [[Forge]] upgrade.
==General==
*Items of Common, Fine, and Superior Quality can be found on the bodies of enemies or in stores throughout ''Tyranny''. Some locked chests will contain the occasional Exquisite item. 
*The only way to obtain a Masterwork item is to improve it yourself (or be really high level).
==Weapon quality==
*Damage increases by roughly 30% (minimum) and 25% (maximum) per quality level.
* Weapons with Accuracy or Armor Penetration bonuses receive an additional +2 [[Accuracy]] and +1 [[Armor Penetration]] per quality level. 
==Shield quality==
* Parry and Dodge bonuses increase by +1 per quality level.
* Endurance bonuses increase every other quality level by +1 (except for iron shields). 
* Recovery penalties are reduced by -0.1s at Superior and Masterwork quality.
==Armor quality==
Bonuses
* Headgear receive +1 (Cloth), +2 (light leather), or +3 (heavy leather) [[Accuracy]] per quality upgrade.
* All gloves receive +2 to Unarmed damage per quality upgrade.
* Leather gloves receive +1 [[Precision]] per quality upgrade, cloth gloves starting with upgrade to Superior quality. 
* All cloth and leather body armor receive +1% [[Deflection]] per quality level.
* Cloth and leather gloves, boots and headgear receive +1% [[Deflection]] at Superior and Masterwork quality.
* All non-cloth body armor receives +1 [[Armor]] per quality level.
* All bronze and iron helmets receive +0.5 [[Armor]] per quality level.
* Items with increased protection against particular types of damage (e.g. bronze armor vs. corroding damage) receive a +25 bonus to that protection.
* Boots receive +1 (cloth), +2 (light leather), or +3 (heavy leather) to disengagement protection per quality level.
[[Recovery]]
* Body armor recovery penalties are reduced only when reaching Exquisite quality. By -0.3s for leather and bronze armor, -0.4 for one made from iron.
** [[Barik]] is an exception, as his body armor receives that bonus at the same rate as other pieces of his armor.
* Gloves, boots and headgear made from bronze and iron receive a -0.1s reduction at Superior and Masterwork quality.
* Gloves, boots and headgear made from leather receive a -0.1s reduction only when reaching Exquisite quality.
** starting Fatebinder's cloth equipment is an exception. It has +0.1 recovery penalty and looses it with upgrade to Fine quality.

{{Infobox item |image = ImperialCopperRing_L.png|Copper ImperialBronzeRing_L.png|Bronze ImperialIronRing_L.png|Iron |type =Legal tender |effect = |cost = |id =money_01_cr (copper)
money_01_br (bronze)
money_01_ir (iron) }} '''Rings''' were first introduced by [[Kyros]] in the early years of the Northern Conquest. The currency of the divided realms was of questionable value and easily counterfeit, and rings offered the promise of a shared economy simple enough for anyone to understand. Today they are the standardized currency across all the known lands of Terratus. Their commonality and ease of transportation quickly made rings the preferred unit of trade even in realms where [[Kyros]]' Peace is not observed. These thin loops of metal are carried on a rope, string, or leather cord worn about the waist or neck. Each ring is not solid - the ends may be pulled apart to remove a ring from the cord and used as payment. There are three metals used in Kyros' ring currency: copper, bronze, and iron (The bronze used in currency is a weaker alloy than that found in bronze weapons and armor). 1 bronze ring is equal to the value of 100 copper rings. 1 iron ring is equal to the value of 100 bronze rings. Early in Kyros' Empire, the weight and value of each ring was standardized. Counterfeiting rings in Kyros' Empire is punishable by death. As rings are used as currency, it is considered vulgar to wear rings as adornment or jewelry. Such decorations are seen as vulgar, and those who wear them are held in contempt. All rings earned in a playthrough will carry over into [[New Game+]]. ==Denominations== * [[File:ImperialIronRing_L.png|30px]] The iron ring is the largest denomination - valued at one hundred bronze rings, or ten thousand copper rings. Only the Forge-Bound of the North know the secret to forging iron in such small and delicate detail, and each of these iron rings is worth more than a peasant's yearly earnings. ({{rings|1||}}={{rings||100|}}={{rings|||10000}}) * [[File:ImperialBronzeRing_L.png|30px]] Made from copper and tin alloy, the bronze ring is valued at one-hundred times the value of the copper ring ({{rings||1|}}={{rings|||100}}) - also known as a hand-of-hands. * [[File:ImperialCopperRing_L.png|30px]] The copper ring is the smallest denomination - making it the base unit of the Overlord's accounting. Traditionally, these are never worn on the hand as jewelry; only during active haggling and counting does one put these on the hand to quickly show groups of fives and tens. '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Bastard's Wound (DLC)|Bastard's Wound]]''.

==Description==
A viciously-sharp bronze blade raggedly-engraved with primitive sigils of some long-forgotten Archon, Rune-Edge came into the possession of House Helos of the Bastard Tier before the rise of the [[bastard city|Bastard City]]. When the Helos family fell to avaricious House Dermecian, one of their champions claimed Rune-Edge as a trophy of war. Since then, it has changed hands no fewer than twenty times, appearing prominently in the histories of several wars between the various kingdoms of the Tiers.
Less than a century ago, importer Norastus Bephos of Azure purchased the sword, only to have his granddaughter sell it to the merchant prince Rostrom Vorus two decades past. Vorus kept the axe prominently displayed in his mountain estate, and he boasted often that Rune-Edge would claim the head of any [[kyros|Kyros]]-sucking northerner who dared try to oust him from his home.
He did not count on the inevitable northern invader being [[cairn|Cairn]].

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
[[sage|Sage]] Litotes,

We can’t help you with the ringing in your ears just yet, so we’ll have to make do until the conflict is over. Yes, Arwel was very explicit in his directives. I know they seem impossible, but that is the situation we face. Everyone that could interpret the Silent Archive died in last night’s attack, so we’re not getting any assistance in this matter. Thankfully, I do have an idea, one which requires everyone’s participation.

Scale is the issue. Steya’s last experiments only affected as much as a small chamber. I believe that we can amplify the spell’s effects by repeating the motions of its sigils as a group, similar to the “ritual” magic used in primitive cultures that pre-dated modern Tiersmen. [[sage|Sage]] Dangling Participle believes that this will create an exponential growth in the spell’s effects, but at an expected cost to stability. I’m inclined to agree. Also, we have no other ideas.

No one else here has your expertise in magical foci. You’ve told me countless times how minor baubles can have a profound leveling effect on spells that exceed the control of their casters. What if we used something as powerful as an artifact as the focus of the ritual? Without one, the energies involved will quickly become chaotic and almost assuredly deadly for all of us. At least with an artifact, there’s a chance that Steya’s spell will encompass the entire Citadel and put it into state of stasis.

In my opinion, there’s only one artifact to use and that’s the Silent Archive itself. It’s clearly the most potent object in this room. [[sage|Sage]] Dangling Participle believes that the Staff of Hours will suffice, but I’m not going to leave anything to chance. Better that we use the Silent Archive as our focus now and figure out how to safely retrieve it later. Nod if you agree after reading this. 

I really hope that blast didn’t take your sight as well.

-[[sage|Sage]] Torven

'''Scales of Mercy''' is an [[artifact]] in ''[[Tyranny]]''.
==Background==
The Scales of Mercy are an expression of the Fatebinder's role inspired by the Court.

Twin pans - engraved with the names JUSTICE and CONFLICT - are perfectly weighted, and tip by an invisible force seemingly when you aren't paying attention. Tunon has been known to grant scales like these as gifts to ambitious pupils, offering no explanation of their function or purpose. They are useless for measuring tangible weight, yet they appear to measure something, as the pans are always in motion. The most Tunon has ever offered by way of an answer was to tell a pupil, "Contemplate the role and your place within it. Are you justice, the hammer it swings, or the pedestal on which it stands?"

Past Fatebinders believed that the riddle has no answer, and Tunon simply wishes each of his pupils to arrive at their own conclusions. Others wondered if Tunon himself seeks an answer, and in observing the progress of his Fatebinders he wages a battle of self-discovery.

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
A red spiral is carved upon the wooden cover of this papyrus notebook. The handwriting within is haphazard and inscrutable - the work of an unpracticed, poorly trained word caster.
A few entries contain recognizable sentences, and the book appears to be the journal of a Scarlet Chorus commander detailing troop movements. Times and locations are noted alongside numbers and pictures of trees, stick figures, and rocks - the author either didn't know the words for lumber, ore, and people or just felt more comfortable with pictures than words. While much of the journal is inscrutable, the corner of every page has the day's headcount for the author's brigade. While some days note dozens of losses, the brigade appears to be recruiting far faster than its members are dying or deserting.

==Description==
The north team returned with a haul of moss and grubs. I remember when live worms made me gag - I miss those days. The east team dredged up some iron blades - much of it rusted and chipped, but a half dozen quality swords were found in the salvage.
We continue to find the bodies of Unbroken. I should be among the dead of the Blade Grave... I should have fought alongside my brethren against the Disfavored. We who were assigned elsewhere, we 'lucky' few, we carry the shame of having been absent when our comrades needed us most. The Scarlet Chorus presence grows steadily. Each moon sees a batch of fresh recruits drawn in from elsewhere. At first I assumed the Scarlet Chorus were here to recruit us by force, but now I believe their motivation is discovery. They have starting taking prisoners - an unusual change of strategy for the Chorus. In the past, they've always 'recruited' those they take alive - readily executing those who refuse to join. Are my soldiers to be used as bait for some upcoming trap? Or are they being kept for the Voices of Nerat's amusement?

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Bastard's Wound (DLC)|Bastard's Wound]]''.

==Description==
This scroll contains a magical Accent which allows a spell to bounce to numerous targets.
==Location==
Sigil of Bounding Bolts III (Greater) dont work. When interact PC add only Sigil of Bounding Bolts II (Normal).


I found a solution to the problem. Using this instruction  https://www.reddit.com/r/TyrannyGame/comments/5cnl2j/how_to_respec_or_edit_character_stats/  and winrar, in the MobileObjects.save file find the lines:
 <Simple value = "m_knownModifiers" />

                      <Collection type = "System.Collections.Generic.List`1 [[SpellModifier, Assembly-CSharp]], mscorlib">

                        <Properties>

                          <Simple name = "Capacity" value = "64" />

                        </Properties>

                        <Items>
and add at the bottom
 <Simple type = "System.String, mscorlib" value = "Assets / Data / Prefabs / VX1 / Items / Misc / vx1_Mod_Chain_III.prefab" />
This method is suitable for anyone who wants to get a new experience on re-play.{{stub}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is an item in ''[[Tyranny]]''.

==Description==
Drawn upon this slip of papyrus is a portrait of Sender Cade that boasts a reasonable likeness to the man in the flesh. A red spiral is inked over Cade's neck. Bereft of words, this is a death notice against Sender Cade - its simple iconography sensible to the illiterate masses of the Scarlet Chorus. Notices like these are disseminated throughout the ranks of the Scarlet Chorus and bounties are paid upon the delivery of a severed head matching the death notice's portrait.

'''Sentinel''' is a [[weapons|weapon]] in ''Tyranny''. 

==Background==
Fighters who live to an advanced age will adopt swords like Sentinel early in their career.
Tradition holds that the wielder etches a tasteful representation of their life's path along the flat of the blade, and anyone who picks it up after their death will know their story. This practice gave way to complicated laws of inheritance, and has faded from popularity.
==Location==
* Manufactured at a [[Forge]] after finding the [[Broken Hilt]]. Requires {{rings||60|}} {{res|||15||}} and 5 recruits.

'''Sigil of Force''' is a Core Sigil in ''Tyranny''.

==Description==
Use the Sigil of Force to channel arcane energy into magical forces that push and knock enemies to the ground.
Many mage guilds throughout the centuries discovered the Sigil of Force, and each held it as a jealously guarded secret. As each was conquered and absorbed into [[Kyros' Empire]], they were chagrined to discover that their 'secret' was the most commonly known piece of arcane lore on Terratus.

== Speculation ==
No known Archon is associated with the Sigil of Force, and given the widespread rediscovery of it, no associated Archon is plausible. This, taken together with the shape of the sigil, suggests the alternate theory that it may be derived from the ''Spires'' rather than from an Archon. This would both explain why it was believed to be a cunningly-deduced secret (since it breaks the normal rules of sigils), but also why it was discovered in so many places (Spires are ubiquitous).

==Location==
* [[Citadel Barracks]]: On the table in the scriptorium.

'''Sigil''' is the catch-all term for a symbol, rune, or glyph used to channel magic. Most often, a sigil is used to refer to the name of an Archon in this context. Spell casting works on the principle that Archons create new magical phenomena, and mages then imitate these powers - it is the Archon's sigil that a mage must invoke to channel that Archon's power.

Proper spell casting uses not only the ''core sigil'' (for example, a ball of fire would need to start with the sigil of the Archon of Fire) but sigils for shape (a 'bolt' sigil in the fireball example) and for various modifications. Skilled mages have been known to uses sigils that prolong, extend, echo, or intensify their spells.
==Mechanics==
In-game, [[Spells]] are made up of at least two sigils: a Core Sigil and an Expression Sigil. Accent and Enhancement Sigils give the spell additional properties. The more sigils a spell contains, the higher the [[Lore]] required to cast it.

Each spell can only have  ''one'' Enhancement Sigil, while Accent Sigils of different categories can be added (and their effects stack).

'''Stacking rules''' : Expression Sigils also determine what beneficial spells can stack with one another.   For example, the ''Gift of the Golem'' spell (Guarded Form expression) will stack with ''Titan's Touch'' (Focused Intent expression) and ''Spectral Blur'' (Focused Intent expression) will stack with ''Mirror Image'' (Guarded Form expression).  But Titan's Touch will ''not'' stack with Spectral Blur as they both use the expression Focused Intent.

All learnt Sigils will carry over into [[New Game+]].

'''Skills''' are the second aspect of ''Tyranny'' 's [[character system]]. The Fatebinder can have a total of 22 skills (6 combat, 5 support and 11 magic), while [[Eb]] and [[Sirin]] can have 23 due to an extra skill which is unique to them. On the flip side, [[Kills-in-Shadow]] can only benefit from 18, as her weapon skills are limited to [[One-Handed Weapons]] and [[Unarmed Combat]].

Each skill is tied to a primary and secondary [[Attributes|attribute]]. These determine the base value of the skill: The primary contributes skill points equal to 1.5 times its value, the secondary 0.5 times.

Skills improve automatically through use and contribute experience to gaining levels. You can spend [[rings]] to train skills by hiring trainers at the [[Mountain Spire]], and Spires where  the [[Training grounds]] and [[Library]] (magic skills) are built.
